title: Draw a line in the sand
coreMove: Pick a belief, then refuse the people it pushes away. A line you live in product, price, and words turns vague preference into a standard that decides for you.

exampleSpecs.audience: founders weighing a big-customer feature request
exampleSpecs.stakes: a contract that would add enterprise bloat
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: refuse a feature that contradicts the public stance against feature overload

exampleSpecs.audience: owners pressured to take every order
exampleSpecs.stakes: a lucrative rush job that violates the shop's standard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: let a turned-away customer clarify the boundary

exampleSpecs.audience: founders tempted to stage a fight for buzz
exampleSpecs.stakes: credibility once buyers inspect the product
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: expose manufactured controversy with no operating belief behind it

exampleSpecs.stakes: a launch with strong reviews but no advocates
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show that zero complaints signaled blandness, not excellence

exampleSpecs.stakes: a stance that changes nothing because no one can see it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: make a private belief visible in pricing and refusal

exampleSpecs.audience: marketers choosing between ads and advocates
exampleSpecs.stakes: growth budget split between paid reach and a stance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show conviction-driven word of mouth beating paid advertising
